q: For a trial of instrumental delivery in theatre, what block is aimed for?
o: A dense block to T4 so conversion to caesarean is immediate
why: Aim for a caesarean-ready block to T4, either by extending the epidural or with a spinal/CSE.

q: What is the normal baseline fetal heart rate on CTG?
why: Normal baseline is 110–160 bpm with variability of 5–25 bpm.

q: What defines a fetal heart rate acceleration?
o: A rise of over 5 bpm for 5 s
A rise of over 15 bpm for 15 s or more
A rise over 30 bpm for 1 minute
why: Accelerations (over 15 bpm for 15 s or more) are a sign of fetal wellbeing.

q: Which CTG finding needs urgent intervention?
why: Acute bradycardia or a prolonged deceleration over 3 minutes needs urgent action.

q: What fetal blood sample pH is normal?
why: Over 7.25 is normal, 7.20–7.25 borderline, under 7.20 abnormal.

q: Which dermatomes carry first stage labour pain?
why: First stage visceral pain travels via T10–L1; second stage perineal pain via the pudendal nerve (S2–4).

q: What remifentanil PCA bolus and lockout are typical in labour?
why: Needs 1:1 midwife care, continuous SpO2 and a dedicated line.

q: What is a common epidural top-up mixture for rapid extension to caesarean?
why: 2% lidocaine with adrenaline and bicarbonate gives a fast, dense block.

q: Which neonatal injury is associated with instrumental (ventouse) delivery?
why: Cephalhaematoma and subgaleal bleeding are recognised after ventouse; failed instrumental increases PPH risk.

q: Which systemic opioid can be given by midwives under exemption for labour?
why: Pethidine (with its active metabolite norpethidine) delays gastric emptying.
